check1_followup: In the spec itself, every critical and high finding from check 1 is fixed: the G07 at-or-below rule, member_count set to warn only while counsel_pending with count_basis defined, the complete parameter table 1a/1b, frozen types and the fact catalogue, registerGateEvaluator with versioned replay, deps on A14/A18/A21 with the worker path, A04 core tables, registerHaltSource and openHalt using A48's rules, G22 row adoption with A12's codes, action_sha256 with assertPassed and the facts ban, the override allow-list, the complete gate-sets table 3, and the hold result. One gap remains outside the spec. The fix for check 1's critical finding also asked for the A19 summary in the graph data to be updated, and that was not done (see finding 6).

findings.issue: The G13 binding with A14 cannot work as written. G13 requires A14's approval payload_sha256 to equal 'the action's canonical hash'. But action_sha256 is defined over a field set that includes approval_id, while A14's payload_sha256 is the hash of the approval's own payload_canonical, which cannot contain its own approval id and uses A14's own field set. The two hashes can never be equal. So G13 either fails every policy-coded action (mint, withdrawal of A$50k or more, transfers, go-live, offer submit, announcements), or the builder quietly compares something weaker, such as object_ref only. That lets an approval for 1 unit authorise a mint of 499. No oracle vector checks for this.
findings.fix: Define two hashes. action_core_sha256 is action_sha256 without approval_id. approvalPayloadFor(ctx) is the per-action-code mapping from an ActionContext to A14's payload_canonical. G13 passes only if every one of these holds: approval.state is approved and not expired or consumed, approval.policy_code equals ctx.policy_code, approval.object_ref equals ctx.object_ref, and approval.payload_sha256 equals sha256(approvalPayloadFor(ctx)). Add oracle vectors for three cases: an approval for 1 unit used for a 499-unit mint fails with G13_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH; an approval for another object fails; an expired approval fails.

findings.issue: The A14 precheck hooks are circular and cannot be mapped. At boot, A19 registers a precheck hook that runs 'the same gate set' as table 3. But the mint, forced_transfer, estate_transfer, recovery, withdrawal, offer_submit, listing_go_live, announcement and tenant_admission rows all contain G13. At precheck time the request is not yet approved, so G13 fails and A14 rejects every such request (A14: a fail hook ends the request 'rejected'). Two more gaps: (a) nothing maps A03's approval action codes to A19's ActionKind, so 'every policy action code whose effect is one of the kinds in table 3' cannot be computed or tested; (b) A14's hook result is pass, warn or fail, and A19's 'held' outcome has no mapping to it.
findings.fix: State that the precheck evaluates the table-3 set with G13 skipped, recorded as not_applicable with reason PRECHECK_G13_DEFERRED and valid only in precheck mode, and that G13 is decided at execution by assertPassed with requireFresh. Add a frozen table in A19 mapping each approval action code (A03 maker-checker rows plus the rules.* codes) to its ActionKind, or have A03 carry an action_kind field. Map outcomes to A14 as passed -> pass, passed_with_warnings -> warn, held -> warn with code RULES_HELD_<gate>, and blocked -> fail. Add oracle vectors: the mint precheck passes with G13 deferred, and every mapped code has a hook.

findings.issue: G02 and G14 have no owner, and the screening-freshness check is enforced by nobody. A19 says A42 registers the G02 evaluator for distribution_line and withdrawal and the G14 evaluator, and that 'A42's evaluator also requires the result to be younger than screening_max_age_h'. A42's frozen spec says the reverse: 'A19 owns the G02 and G14 verdicts; this node supplies facts only. It registers no evaluator.' Table 1b makes screening_max_age_h an A42 policy row, while A42 says it is A19's parameter and defines none, so the parameter has no home. A42's fact outcome vocabulary (clear | review | not_applicable_in_phase | unavailable) and its SCREENING_UNAVAILABLE code are also missing from A19's fact catalogue and G02 text. As a result, a payout or withdrawal on a screening result days old passes A19's baseline G02. A32 has the same inversion for G04 and G05 ('A19 owns the G04 and G05 evaluators').
findings.fix: Make A19's baseline evaluators final for G02, G14, G04 and G05, and remove A42 and A32 from the registerGateEvaluator list. Move screening_max_age_h (hours, default 24, counsel_pending with the MLRO) into table 1a as aml.screening_max_age_h and drop it from table 1b. Update G02's fact type to {outcome: clear|review|not_applicable_in_phase|unavailable, screened_at, subjects[]} with these results: review -> fail SCREENING_HIT_OPEN; unavailable -> fail SCREENING_UNAVAILABLE; not_applicable_in_phase -> neutral in P1 and P2; any payout kind with screened_at older than the parameter -> fail SCREENING_STALE. Add oracle vectors for each case, including a withdrawal screened 25 hours earlier.

findings.issue: AML tipping-off leak. Under s123 of the AML/CTF Act, a customer must not learn of a suspicion or an SMR. Product map M20 says 'Operator-only, so no one can tip off a customer', and A42 requires the investor-facing A19 verdicts for withdrawal, order and distribution_line to carry no case data and to be byte-identical (after id substitution) for restricted and unrestricted investors, shown only as under_review. A19 has no redaction. GET evaluations/{setId} is open to 'the subject, their agents, the owning tenant', the buy stepper shows each failed gate's fix-it, and the reason codes SCREENING_HIT_OPEN and G14_RESTRICTED would reach the investor, their AI agent through the API and MCP, and the sponsor.
findings.fix: Add output shaping for evaluation sets and verdicts, as the simulator already has. For the subject, their agents and tenant principals, G02 and G14 results that are not pass are replaced by one neutral verdict {result: hold, reason_codes: ['UNDER_REVIEW'], fix_it: 'gate.under_review'} with no case, restriction or screening fields. facts_canonical and the raw reason codes are visible only to M10 and M20 staff scopes. G14's TTR warning is never shown to the investor. Add an oracle vector: the investor-, agent- and sponsor-shaped responses for a restricted investor and an unrestricted investor who is under review are byte-identical, and neither contains 'AML', 'sanction', 'SCREENING' or 'G14_RESTRICTED'.

findings.issue: Approved rule changes have no executor, and one change path has no approval code, so maker-checker on M10 can be bypassed. A14 applies approved changes only through each owning module's registerEffector(action_code, {execute, revert, postcondition}), but A19 registers no effector for rules.pack.change, rules.override.create, rules.lockup.set or rules.monitor.pretrade_block. Nothing says what moves a pack to approved_pending_effect or effective, or an override to approved. The builder is therefore free to flip states from the route after reading the approval row. Separately, 'PUT vehicles/{id}/compliance-rule (draft, then A14)' names no action code or policy, and a per-vehicle holder_cap_bps has no bound, so a vehicle cap could be set at or above the 20% landholder threshold. The only bound, 1000 bps, applies to investor overrides. No oracle vector proves that a pack, rule, override or pre-trade block cannot take effect without an approved, hash-matching A14 request.
findings.fix: Register A14 effectors (execute, revert, postcondition) for rules.pack.change, rules.compliance_rule.change (new, CCO maker and LEGL checker per ADM-16 'Change rule parameter'), rules.override.create, rules.lockup.set and rules.monitor.pretrade_block. Only an effector may change these rows' state, and a DB trigger or module guard refuses a state change without an approval_id in state approved. Add compliance_rule.holder_cap_bps_max = 1000 to table 1a, below the lowest landholder threshold, with a validation code. Add oracle vectors: a pack with no approval, or with a rejected or expired approval, never becomes effective; a vehicle cap above the maximum is refused.

findings.issue: The fix for check 1's critical finding is incomplete outside the spec. The A19 summary in both app-graph.json and final-graph.json still says 'a 500-token order failing G07 naming the maximum allowed', which contradicts the spec's at-or-below rule (500 passes, 501 fails). It also says 'Gates not yet backed by a service (G05, G09, G15) return not applicable in this phase', which contradicts the spec and its own phase-leakage challenge, since G05 must fail G05_PHASE_OFF for retail in P1. It still says G22 is 'registered from the agent-authority package' rather than adapted, and 's601ED member count (default 20)'. final-graph.json still lists deps [A09, A03, A12] without A14, A18 and A21. The orchestrator passes this summary to the builder and to Fable as node data, so an oracle written from it would encode the wrong G07 boundary and G05 result.
findings.fix: Update the A19 summary in app-graph.json and final-graph.json now; do not defer it to Specify. Use: '...G07 at or below the cap (500 of 10,000 passes, 501 fails naming 500); G05 fails G05_PHASE_OFF for retail in P1, and G09 and G15 are not_applicable in this phase; G21 and G22 are adapters over A21 and A12; s601ED member count warns (trigger > 20, counsel pending)...'. Add A14, A18 and A21 to final-graph.json deps and regenerate. Mark the design-analysis note at line 321 ('>= 500 tokens fails') as superseded.

findings.issue: The Unlocks list and the gate step disagree with the graph. The spec lists nine dependents and says 'Pass unlocks the nine dependents', but app-graph.json has twelve: A17, A35 and A104 are also dependents. A104 (the MCP server) generates tools from these routes, and A17 and A35 register fact providers.
findings.fix: Add A17, A35 and A104 to Unlocks and change 'nine' to 'twelve', or derive the count from the graph.

findings.issue: The halt hand-over to A48 has no mechanism. The spec says that 'from A48 on' openHalt and closeHalt become forwarders and that A48 replaces the 'halts' source. But A48 cannot edit A19's owned paths, and A19 defines no way to swap the backend. It also does not say what registerHaltSource does when a name is already registered, and A48 registers the same name, 'halts'. A48 also calls A19's table 'halts', while A19 uses A04's 'halt' table.
findings.fix: Export registerHaltBackend({open, close}) from index.ts; once A48 registers it, openHalt and closeHalt delegate to it. Define that registerHaltSource(name) with an existing name replaces the earlier source only when called with {replace: true} by the owning node, and otherwise throws HALT_SOURCE_DUPLICATE. Add a test that after A48's registration the local table receives no rows. Record the table name 'halt' for A48's reconciliation.

findings.issue: The lock-ups effector calls a downstream node. 'Set lock-up dates ... asks A28 for the on-chain partial freeze', but A28 (AM2) depends on A19 through its own ancestors and is not a dependency, so A19 cannot import it. Either the build breaks or the on-chain freeze is silently skipped, which leaves the register and the chain inconsistent for R6.
findings.fix: Have the lock-up effector set lot dates through A18 and emit the outbox event rules.lockup.set {vehicle_id, lots, release_date, approval_id}. A28 consumes it and performs the partial freeze, and A20 detects any mismatch between the register and the chain. Add a test that the event is emitted in the same transaction.

findings.issue: Re-evaluating G22 conflicts with A12. A12's frozen criterion is 'exactly one gate_evaluation row for G22' per token request, but A19 writes a second G22 row when 'the vehicle, amount or units differ' within the request. When A19 evaluates G22 by itself (a later job, or requireFresh), it runs the pure evaluateG22 without A12's counter reservation, so an agent action executed later or at a larger amount does not count toward the daily or monthly caps. Nothing maps A12's CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED (per-action cap on a confirmable cell) to a GateResult.
findings.fix: Inside a token request, if the action differs from the route's G22 input, refuse with RULES_G22_ACTION_MISMATCH and never write a second row. Outside a request, call A12's reservation port (reserve or release under the counter lock) together with evaluateG22. Map CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED to hold G22_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, carrying confirmation_id and cap. Add oracle vectors for all three cases.

findings.issue: D04 attribution for M10 changes is implicit. The audit rule for pack, rule, override, lock-up, pre-trade and halt changes records the approval_id but does not say that an agent maker is recorded as 'agent <token> on behalf of <person>' (token_id and on_behalf_of_id), and no test checks it.
findings.fix: State that every audit event and every rules.* approval request made through an agent token carries actor_type AGNT, token_id and on_behalf_of_id. Add a test with a CCO agent drafting an override.

findings.issue: The wholesale citations point to Chapter 6D. Units in a managed investment scheme are offered under Part 7.9, where the wholesale-client tests are s761G(7)(a) (A$500k), s761G(7)(c) with reg 7.1.28 (the accountant's certificate), s761GA (sophisticated investor) and s761G(7)(d) (professional investor). The s708(8), (9) and (10) references in table 1a are the Chapter 6D equivalents. The values are right, but the sources are not.
findings.fix: Cite s761G(7) and reg 7.1.28 as the primary sources, keep s708 as a cross-reference, and add a note for counsel.
